Triggers.value: Visible injuries or wounds on others

Threat.value: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I wake during the night to check whether I am safe

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop

Negative Appraisals.value: You can never know who will harm you
I can't trust that I will do the right thing
I have permanently changed for the worse

vignette: María, a 27-year-old Latin American woman working as an HVAC technician, has been struggling with the aftermath of a traumatic event that occurred several months ago. María was kidnapped and subjected to severe torture by individuals who falsely accused her of crimes she did not commit. The experience left deep emotional scars and triggered intense psychological reactions. Since the incident, María’s life has become a series of cautious routines and avoidances, shaped by constant vigilance and fear. Being alone with women is particularly distressing for María; this stems from an episode during her captivity where other female prisoners were present, contributing to her sense of vulnerability and entrapment. This trigger now manifests in her daily work life, where she avoids one-on-one interactions with female clients or colleagues. The visual presence of injuries or wounds on others also triggers intense reactions in María. She recounts a time when she was asked to service an air conditioning unit at a local hospital. The sight of patients with visible injuries in the waiting area caused her to feel overwhelming distress, leading her to abruptly leave the job site. This reaction further intensified her sense of entrapment and lack of control. María’s daily routine is marked by repeated checking behaviors. She frequently checks that doors and windows are securely locked, even in environments where she previously felt safe. At night, she wakes up several times to ensure that everything remains secure. This hyper-vigilance has made her nights restless and fragmented, leaving her exhausted during the day. She describes feeling jumpy and easily startled by sudden movements or sounds. A colleague walking into her workspace unexpectedly can send her into a panic. The constant state of alertness is both exhausting and isolating for María. She had come to believe that “you can never know who will harm you,” which further fuels her anxiety. María’s memories of the traumatic event are fragmented and often feel alien to her, as if they belong to someone else rather than herself. This detachment is particularly evident when she recalls specific moments from captivity, which flood her with intense shame and emotional overwhelm. She often has to pause whatever she is doing to process these emotions, causing delays in her work and personal tasks. Negative appraisals have taken root in María’s thoughts, shaping how she views herself and the world around her. She experiences significant self-doubt about her ability to make sound decisions and fears that she will never be able to trust anyone again. These beliefs have led her to isolate further from others, as she believes she can’t rely on anyone for support or safety. The cumulative effect of these symptoms has impacted María’s work and personal life significantly. She has begun to miss deadlines at work due to her frequent need to check locks and windows, leading to strained relationships with colleagues. Her social circle has dwindled, as she avoids interactions that might trigger her fears or anxieties. What finally brought María to seek help was a particularly distressing incident where she felt overwhelmed by memories while working alone in a client’s home. She was convinced that the door had been tampered with, even though it appeared secure. This episode left her feeling entirely helpless and further eroded her sense of self-worth. María is most afraid of being trapped again and losing control over her life. However, she also hopes for a way to regain trust in herself and others, to find peace in her memories rather than feel controlled by them. She seeks help with the hope that understanding these triggers and behaviors can lead to a more stable and fulfilling life.
